question: Should OpenClaw adopt this private shared localization-core runtime and the five-PR cross-surface rollout as the supported product direction before reviewing the implementation series for merge?
rationale: The proposal establishes a new foundation spanning UI, CLI, Gateway metadata, and approval presentation; the linked RFC is open and the supplied review context shows no maintainer decision accepting that permanent contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed foundation
options.body: Confirm the internal runtime boundary and the first landing scope, then require the branch to remove release-owned changelog text and supply focused runtime and upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause for RFC resolution
options.body: Keep the draft series unmerged until the RFC establishes ownership, supported surfaces, and the intended long-term localization contract.

options.title: Prefer existing per-surface localization
options.body: Decline the shared runtime direction and keep localization ownership in existing UI, onboarding, and channel-specific seams.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed foundation
recommendation.body: Confirm the internal runtime boundary and the first landing scope, then require the branch to remove release-owned changelog text and supply focused runtime and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed author of the linked RFC and the prior/current localization foundation proposals.
